lemonde.description: Alors que les frappes américaines se poursuivent en Iran, le pouvoir iranien évite, pour l’instant, une confrontation totale. Son calcul repose sur la menace de provoquer une perturbation énergétique mondiale pour contraindre Washington à revoir sa stratégie.

lemonde.title: Le projet de loi d’urgence agricole adopté dans la cacophonie par une Assemblée nationale fracturée sur la question des pesticides
lemonde.description: ​Le gouvernement craignait que la mesure permettant la réautorisation dérogatoire de deux néonicotinoïdes, ajoutée par le Sénat, ne conduise au rejet du texte. Le projet de loi a finalement été largement adopté par les députés dans la nuit de lundi à mardi par 296 voix pour, majoritairement issues de la droite et de l’extrême droite et 224 contre.

lemonde.description: Notre reporter s’est rendue pour « Le Monde Afrique » avec le photographe Philémon Barbier à Mongbwalu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, où l’épidémie d’Ebola due à la souche Bundibugyo s’est déclarée et progresse rapidement. lemonde.description: Le nombre de réfugiés ukrainiens dans le monde (hors Russie) s’élevait à 5,762 millions de personnes au 30 avril 2026, dont 5,213 millions enregistrés en Europe et 549 000 hors du continent, selon le dernier bulletin mensuel du ministère de l’économie et de l’environnement d’Ukraine, qui cite les données du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés.

lemonde.title: Interruption du concert de Barbara Butch à Grenoble : la maire écologiste, Laurence Ruffin, dénonce la « stratégie d’intimidation » des « insoumis »
lemonde.description: La DJ était visée par un appel au boycott des élus « insoumis » pour avoir signé une tribune de soutien à la proposition de loi « visant à lutter contre les formes renouvelées d’antisémitisme ». Elle a dû interrompre son concert, samedi 18 juillet, à Grenoble, alors qu’une centaine de militants propalestiniens étaient venus manifester contre sa présence.

lemonde.title: « Un corps noir dans un espace blanc, c’est un accident industriel » : la peau, un nuancier de discriminations au travail

Le Parlement français vote mardi ce texte porté par Emmanuel Macron, qui entrera en vigueur dès septembre. Les plateformes devront vérifier l'âge des utilisateurs, sans sanction prévue pour les familles

C'est la première fois que le ministère de la Défense nippon repère un exercice de tir réel de la Chine dans la ZEE du Japon. Tokyo a contacté Pékin pour lui faire savoir que cet exercice «aurait pu mettre en danger la navigation des navires se trouvant à proximité»

letemps.description:

OPINION. Réagissant à un appel à cesser les licenciements à la SSR, à laquelle le peuple a montré son attachement le 8 mars, le directeur de la RTS, Pascal Crittin, rappelle qu’ils sont dus à la réduction de la redevance décidée par le Conseil fédéral

letemps.description:
Les régions septentrionales de Coquimbo et d'Atacama sont touchées, depuis le 15 juillet, par d'intenses précipitations qui ont coupé les routes et isolé près de 100 000 personnes. Quelque 2422 personnes ont vu leurs domiciles gravement endommagés

observador.title: "Encarregados de educação podem ter direito a indemnizações"
observador.description: Bastonário da Ordem dos Advogados diz que é possível se pais conseguirem provar nexo causalidade. Mesmo assim, agora, afirma que o ideal é optar pela via administrativa através da revisão das provas.

observador.title: "Não vejo uma reforma profunda do Estado a acontecer"
observador.description: João Moreira Rato sublinha que a mudança real exige ir além de planos teóricos e focar na complexidade da execução pública. O país ainda carece de uma transformação estrutural nas suas instituições?

observador.title: 10h. Primeiro-ministro não vai tirar férias no verão
observador.description: Luís Montenegro vai estar a "coordenar a atividade do Governo" e vai manter agenda como presidente do PSD. Ainda, o ministro da Educação é ouvido na Assembleia da República.

observador.title: Gestora de fundos Arrow adquire hotel e casino de Tróia
observador.description: Uma sociedade do grupo Arrow pretende adquirir mais ativos em Tróia. Chegou a acordo para ficar com o hotel e o casino da Península, alargando a sua presença.

observador.title: Exames: o Ministro perdeu mesmo o resto das folhas?
observador.description: Com exames num caos total e Seguro a esquivar-se a vítimas, Portugal parece um teste sem a última página. Soma-se combustíveis caros e o interior sem multibancos: é a festa da desordem.

observador.title: PSP detém vigilante por tráfico de droga na Nazaré
observador.description: Um vigilante de segurança privada foi detido por suspeita de venda de doses de cocaína no local que patrulhava. A PSP apreendeu 9,37 gramas de droga e 1.780 euros em dinheiro.

observador.title: 9h. 23 concelhos do interior em perigo máximo de incêndio
observador.description: A informação é do IPMA e abrange concelhos dos distritos de Vila Real, Bragança, Guarda, Castelo Branco e Faro. Ainda, a Rússia atacou a Ucrânia na passada madrugada com quase 60 drones.

observador.title: Volta. Caça ao lixo tem "tendência a diminuir", diz SDR
observador.description: Sistema de recolha de embalagens cumpre três meses com taxa de recolha de 38%. SDR diz que apanha em contentores não reflete "falha" e lembra que valor do depósito não reverte para o Estado.

observador.title: Portugal entre destinos favorecidos por mudanças no turismo
observador.description: Estudo da consultora norte-americana indica que instabilidade geopolítica leva viajantes a "reavaliar destinos e rotas". Apesar disso, poucos cancelam. Segurança também é fator de peso.

observador.title: O estado da Nação sem gritos
observador.description: Os portugueses dizem que estão pior do que há um ano. Como o emprego e o rendimento têm crescido, as razões para esta visão está nos detalhes, onde encontramos em geral o diabo.

observador.title: As notas de graça e o cão que quer matar o Herman
observador.description: Entre o aquecimento espanhol e as vinganças no Parlamento, há alunos a celebrar notas suspensas. Portugal só perde com campeões e o Herman foge do "criminoso" Álvaro.

observador.title: Canadá pronto para "intensificar" negociações com Trump
observador.description: Mark Carney condenou as tarifas adicionais de 50% aos bens importados do Canadá, que "violam diretamente" o Acordo Estados Unidos-México-Canadá. Taxas vão desde "vinho a tacos de hóquei e cimento".

observador.title: Quase 100 militares norte-americanos feridos em duas semanas
observador.description: Sean Parnell diz que a "grande maioria" teve "concussões leves" e que 96% já regressou ao serviço. A confirmação vem depois das mortes de três soldados norte-americanos no último fim de semana.

observador.title: Vá lá: cá está uma coisa que o ministro da Educação fez bem
observador.description: O ministro da Educação (que não acredita em borlas), o ministro da Educação (que teve mais trapalhadas) e os entraves à concorrência (que são muitos) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Segunda fase dos exames arranca: alunos continuam incertos
observador.description: Prova de Português do 9.º e 12.º ano decorre às 9h30, apesar do ceticismo dos alunos: "As notas que foram lançadas, muito provavelmente, estão erradas". Segunda fase termina sexta-feira.

observador.title: Vinte e três concelhos em perigo máximo de incêndio
observador.description: IPMA afirma que o perigo de incêndio vai-se intensificar em algumas regiões a partir de quarta-feira. Prevê céu pouco nublado ou limpo no continente. Máximas entre 24 e 34ºC.

observador.title: Praias privadas: mais uma polémica de Verão ou uma ameaça?
observador.description: Depois dos chapéus de sol, das bolas de Berlim e dos nudistas, as praias privadas aquecem o Verão. O enredo legal é de tal monta que se recomenda juntar um manual de Direito aos óculos de sol.

observador.title: Trincão a ganhar mais do que os campeões mundiais?
observador.description: Com a Federação Espanhola a lucrar milhões, o contrato de Trincão consegue ser mais impressionante. Entre recordes de Rodri e fiascos musicais, a corrida pela Bola de Ouro nunca esteve tão renhida.

elpais.title: La ‘vía Aldama’ se abre paso en el ‘caso Zapatero’: los empresarios desmontan la defensa del expresidente
elpais.description: El exmandatario se desvinculó del rescate de la aerolínea y negó haber cobrado por ello, lo contrario de lo que aseguran Martínez Martínez, Martínez Sola y Roselli en sus escritos entregados a la Audiencia Nacional

elpais.title: El horizonte judicial de Zapatero pende de la declaración ante el juez de Julio Martínez tras su decisión de “colaborar”
elpais.description: El comisionista declara este martes tras implicar al expresidente en las gestiones del rescate de Plus Ultra

elpais.title: Madrid ruge con la segunda estrella de España
elpais.description: Casi dos millones de personas tiñen de rojo las calles de la capital para abrazar a los campeones del mundo en un día para la historia

elpais.description: Con 19 años y aspecto de alevín, el zaguero del Barça se ha convertido en el mejor joven de un Mundial en el que España solo encajó un gol

elpais.title: Argentina se queda huérfana
elpais.description: La Albiceleste empieza a procesar el cierre de un ciclo dorado, en el que contó con Maradona y Messi en diez de los últimos 12 Mundiales

elpais.title: La nueva ley del tabaco prohíbe fumar a los menores y hacerlo en terrazas y campus universitarios
elpais.description: El Consejo de Ministros aprueba este martes el proyecto, que equipara cigarrillos tradicionales, vapeadores y bolsas de nicotina

elpais.description: El ministerio acelera la criba de suministradoras fantasma que figuran en el registro de la CNMC: 504, de las cuales 130 carecen de actividad. Una nueva normativa ha endurecido las condiciones económicas a estas empresas

elpais.title: Spencer Tunick lleva sus desnudos colectivos a Canarias: “Hay demasiado odio hacia la gente de mente abierta”
elpais.description: El fotógrafo neoyorquino, conocido por sus imágenes casi abstractas de masas de personas desnudas, planea una acción en Gran Canaria en apoyo de los derechos del colectivo LGTBIQA+

elpais.title: De los no nacidos (y de los todavía vivos)
elpais.description: Hay que defender la ingenuidad frente al optimismo y recordar sus fuentes: los niños, el trabajo y la belleza

elpais.description: A veces no queda otra que dejarse llevar. Y eso lo entiende cualquier imbécil

elpais.description: El presunto agresor, de 48 años, está hospitalizado. La víctima no se encontraba en el sistema VioGén

elpais.title: El silencio habita Muriel tras la evacuación por el fuego
elpais.description: “Vives en un sitio privilegiado, muy bonito, pero el riesgo siempre lo tienes en la cabeza”, confiesa un vecino desalojado por el incendio de La Mierla

elpais.title: Macroincendios en Guadalajara, Zaragoza, Almería: ¿nos tenemos que acostumbrar a esto?
elpais.description: En 2026 ya ha habido 15 grandes incendios de más de 500 hectáreas, destacando la letalidad del de Los Gallardos. Va a ir a más por el cambio climático, y vecinos y administraciones tienen que planificar esta nueva normalidad

elpais.title: Comienza la tercera ola de calor del verano, con lo peor en el este y en el sur de la Península
elpais.description: Durará solo tres días y no será especialmente intensa, pero afectará a casi todo el país: solo se librarán la cornisa cantábrica y Canarias

elpais.title: Hispania vaciada: vestigios romanos de pequeñas localidades se convierten en motores de desarrollo rural
elpais.description: Municipios que hoy cuentan con una población mínima se apoyan en su esplendor imperial para resurgir

elpais.title: Una jueza propone sentar en el banquillo a dos ultraderechistas por atacar con explosivos la sede del PSOE de Santander durante una charla
elpais.description: La magistrada vincula a ambos procesados con La Falange y el partido pide casi 15 años de cárcel

elpais.title: Trump aprueba nuevos aranceles del 50% para Canadá en plenas negociaciones por el TMEC
elpais.description: El presidente alega un trato discriminatorio a algunos productos estadounidenses. Pagarán el gravamen materiales de automoción, productos lácteos y bebidas alcohólicas

elpais.title: La muerte de un niño de ocho años por el disparo de un policía conmociona Perú
elpais.description: El caso desata las críticas a la nueva ley que permite que policías y militares acusados de delitos sean juzgados en tribunales castrenses en vez de ordinarios

nyt.title: Inside Andy Burnham’s 1st Day as U.K. Prime Minister
nyt.description: As Andy Burnham became Britain’s seventh leader in a decade on Monday, he tried to show that he will govern differently.

nyt.title: UK’s New Prime Minister Burnham Orders Cut in Taxes on Electricity
nyt.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham moved quickly to confront the high cost of living. And President Trump wished him well after a phone call between the two leaders.

nyt.title: Andy Burnham, New UK Prime Minister, Names John Healey As Top Finance Official
nyt.description: As chancellor, John Healey, who quit as defense secretary in the former government, will fill one of the most consequential posts, overseeing fiscal and economic policy.

nyt.title: G.O.P. Boxed In on Iran War as Trump Sidelines Congress
nyt.description: Republicans now face a worst-case political scenario of being asked to fund an unpopular war over which they have exercised little oversight.

nyt.title: Trump to Impose 50% Tariff on Many Canadian Goods
nyt.description: The administration will use an untested legal provision to put significant duties on Canadian exports, reigniting a clash with one of America’s biggest trading partners.

nyt.title: Trump Rejected Nearly 6,000 Clemency Applications Amid Hope of Pardon Wave
nyt.description: Expectations were raised for a raft of pardons in connection with the country’s 250th birthday but the president granted fewer than 20 on July 3.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Sought Phone Records of Times Journalists and Their Relatives
nyt.description: The government is aggressively seeking the confidential sources of Times reporters who wrote about the president’s new Air Force One. The Times has asked a judge to quash the subpoenas.

nyt.title: The Sewer Knows What You Ate
nyt.description: During the Covid-19 pandemic, wastewater testing became a virus warning system. Now, scientists are using the approach to understand how communities eat.

nyt.title: Lindsey Graham’s Sister, Darline Graham, Says She Will Run to Succeed Him
nyt.description: Ms. Graham, who filled her brother’s Senate seat in South Carolina after his death, does not appear to have previous political experience. But she does have President Trump’s endorsement.

nyt.title: 5 Things to Know About the Maine Senate Candidate Troy Jackson
nyt.description: Mr. Jackson, who has emerged as the clear front-runner to replace Graham Platner, is a Republican turned Democrat who is seen as close to Mr. Platner on policy.

nyt.title: Will a Sex Scandal Involving Mark Lamb Matter in Arizona GOP House Primary?
nyt.description: The contest in a deeply religious part of the state is a test of the power of a Trump endorsement.

nyt.title: How Trump’s Immigration Crackdown Is Hurting Elder Care
nyt.description: Retirement communities already grappling with labor shortages are being forced to terminate caregivers at a time when more Americans are living longer.

nyt.title: Judge Tosses Justice Department Challenge to Minnesota Immigration Laws
nyt.description: The Trump administration, which flooded Minnesota with immigration agents this year, argued that policies limiting cooperation with ICE were unconstitutional.

nyt.title: Spain Celebrates Both a Soccer Win and a Sense of Wider Success
nyt.description: For many fans, the World Cup victory cemented a belief that something promising — a cultural, economic and sports revival — is happening in the country.

nyt.title: Evacuees of Ontario’s Wildfires Wait and Worry
nyt.description: Flames crept, and then sprinted, toward unsuspecting residents who fled remote parts of northwestern Ontario. Now they want to know why officials weren’t prepared.

nyt.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Forms Near the Gulf Coast
nyt.description: Bertha, the second named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season, is expected to drop heavy rain in the region this week.

nyt.title: Wildfire Smoke Gives Way to Powerful Thunderstorms in the Midwest and Northeast
nyt.description: The Midwest and the Northeast are facing potentially intense thunderstorms Monday and Tuesday.

nyt.title: Soaring Egg Prices Are Hitting China Hard
nyt.description: China consumes more eggs per capita than almost every other country, so a recent spike in costs is touching a nerve.

npr.title: Spain's World Cup champions return home for parade in front of almost 2 million
npr.description: The players and their coaching staff met with the country's royals, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. An estimated crowd of almost 2 million was on hand to greet the squad through the streets of Madrid.

npr.title: Powerball ticket sales begin Tuesday in the United Kingdom
npr.description: Powerball ticket sales in the United Kingdom will begin Tuesday, giving players across the Atlantic a chance at winning the same massive jackpot that U.S. players already play for.

npr.title: The war in Iran has left hundreds of U.S. diplomats in limbo
npr.description: As the U.S-Iran war ramps up again, hundreds of diplomats are in limbo. The State Department drew down staffing due to Iran's attacks on Gulf states. It's unclear if they'll return to normal business.

npr.title: The war with Iran is escalating. What next?
npr.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution about the U.S. war with Iran, the increase in hostilities and what it means for the wider region

npr.title: India's Gen Z 'Cockroach People's Party' started as satire but is serious about change
npr.description: They call themselves the "cockroaches" and they're on the march — demanding action against corruption, amid a shortage of opportunities for young people in India.

npr.title: Putin meets North Korean foreign minister in diplomatic push
npr.description: The visit by North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui comes without an obvious occasion, such as a multilateral diplomatic event or state anniversary, and has raised speculation that she may be coordinating a possible visit to Russia by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

npr.title: 3 U.S. personnel killed in Iran conflict. And, Hunter Biden opens up to NPR
npr.description: Three U.S. service members have been killed since Friday amid rising tension between the U.S. and Iran. And, Hunter Biden talks to NPR's Newsmakers about addiction and public scrutiny.

npr.title: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak
npr.description: Congo's health ministry said the deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday. Thirty-seven new deaths were recorded in the previous 24 hours in one of the highest totals.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran launch new strikes after 3 U.S. service members are killed
npr.description: The U.S. attacks were the ninth consecutive day of bombing since peace talks between the two countries collapsed in dispute over a memorandum of understanding focused on the Strait of Hormuz.

npr.title: Andy Burnham becomes U.K. prime minister
npr.description: In a transition of power presided over by King Charles, Andy Burnham has replaced Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister. Both are from the center-left Labour Party.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

phys-org.title: Indigenous knowledge key to building healthier and more sustainable food systems
phys-org.description: Traditional and Indigenous knowledge could play a vital role in addressing some of the world's most pressing challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss and poor health and nutrition, according to a new review of current research.

phys-org.title: Great Barrier Reef at risk of 'collapse', scientists warn
phys-org.description: Australia's Great Barrier Reef is at very high risk of extreme and widespread bleaching and "ecosystem collapse" linked to this year's El Niño weather phenomenon, leading scientists warned Tuesday.

phys-org.title: Fires in Brazil's Amazon dropped to historic low in 2025
phys-org.description: Forest fires in the Brazilian Amazon fell to a historic low in 2025 after peaking the previous year, according to a report published Tuesday.

phys-org.title: Memorable visuals drive online ad purchases more than emotion, study suggests
phys-org.description: A study of digital advertising in the International Journal of Business and Systems Research suggests that memorable visuals are more likely to encourage consumers to buy than campaigns that rely primarily on emotional impact. The findings challenge conventional wisdom about how online advertising influences behavior.

phys-org.title: Envisioning the next 150 years of crop research with the Alma Mater Plots
phys-org.description: A couple of miles south of the main quad at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, a remarkable agricultural experiment is taking shape. The so-called Alma Mater Plots are unique in their setup—with 64 plots of 1 acre (0.4 hectares) each, individually tile-drained, it is the largest experiment of its kind anywhere. To maximize the experiment's value to Illinois and Midwest agriculture, scientists are teaming up with farmers to decide what, exactly, to study.

phys-org.title: Q&A: How anaerobic digestion can help reduce emissions and increase income streams
phys-org.description: An advanced technology that could benefit farmers' bottom line and help meet the rising demand for domestic energy production borrows a key ingredient from a centuries-old practice of burning dried manure to warm homes where trees were sparse or expensive: animal waste.

phys-org.title: Eight lifesaving ways to improve wildfire risk management
phys-org.description: As the flames advanced toward the village of Bédar in Spain's Almería province, the mayor gave a desperate order to ring the church bells to warn residents. It was not enough. The July 9 Los Gallardos fire, which claimed 13 lives and burned 7,000 hectares (17,300 acres), was Spain's third-deadliest on record.

phys-org.title: Decade of research reshapes multilingual learner policy
phys-org.description: A lot of high school students load up on Advanced Placement courses to strengthen their college applications. But for many California students classified as English learners, access to even the basic college-preparatory courses required for admission to the state's public universities can remain out of reach.

phys-org.title: Students enable widespread water monitoring in India
phys-org.description: When a local community gets involved in environmental monitoring, its efforts can build awareness of local environmental issues and provide more abundant data than scientists can collect on their own. But how does the quality of the data compare with readings taken by professionals?

phys-org.title: Unusual three-way bestows magnetic sense to single-celled organism
phys-org.description: How do microorganisms orient themselves to find the optimal habitat? Scientists have thoroughly investigated so-called magnetotactic bacteria, which use the Earth's magnetic field as a biological compass. Some eukaryotic single-celled organisms—that is, more complex organisms like ciliates, which, unlike bacteria, have a cell nucleus—also possess this capability. But how they acquire it has largely remained a puzzle.

phys-org.title: One idea, two cosmic mysteries—linking Little Red Dots and globular clusters
phys-org.description: A new study led by astronomers at The University of Texas at Austin proposes a theory that could solve two astronomical riddles at once: the nature of Little Red Dots and the origin of globular clusters. Rather than representing distinct objects, the study suggests that one may instead be the ancestor of the other: Little Red Dots are, in fact, an early form of globular clusters. The findings are published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

phys-org.title: Transforming vibrations into clean fuels and chemicals through piezosynthesis
phys-org.description: From ocean waves and flowing rivers to the systems used to transport and treat water, vibrations are everywhere. But can vibrations do more than just shake water? Can they split water or drive the production of useful chemicals from water? phys-org.title: New cell imaging method measures protein folding in living organelles
phys-org.description: Protein aggregates are associated with the development of diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. These are found more often in certain areas of cells known as membraneless organelles. Do these organelles promote this protein clumping, or do they protect the cell by temporarily absorbing the aggregates? Professor Simon Ebbinghaus and Mailin Becker from Ruhr University Bochum, Germany, set out to answer this question with their new, self-developed method, "confocal Fast Relaxation Im

phys-org.title: 'Narcissist' bosses are more likely to oppose work from home, studies show. But are they right?
phys-org.description: Have you ever wondered why your boss wants you back in the office full-time, rather than allowing hybrid work, where you can combine work from home and in an office? A fascinating study just shed fresh light on this topic.

phys-org.title: 30,000 people tried for bigamy over the past 400 years in England and Wales, archives reveal
phys-org.description: Bigamy has been a rare crime during the past 400 years—and offenders have been harshly punished. It seems likely that no more than 30,000 individuals have ever been tried for bigamy in England and Wales during this period. Most have been convicted, and possible punishment has ranged from execution, branding, whipping, transportation and imprisonment to fines and community service in more recent decades.

phys-org.title: Molecules stop carbon nanotubes clumping, unlocking record heat-to-electricity performance
phys-org.description: QUT researchers have overcome a challenge that has limited next-generation energy-harvesting materials for more than two decades, opening the door to more powerful wearable electronics and new ways of turning wasted heat into electricity. The breakthrough centers on carbon nanotubes, which are flexible, conductive microscopic rods that have long shown promise for wearable technologies but have been difficult to control.

phys-org.title: Carbon nanotube model reveals how smart sensors perform at aircraft-like extremes
phys-org.description: Researchers from Skoltech, in collaboration with the Harbin Institute of Technology and Jiangsu University (China), have published a study presenting the first empirical model to explain and predict the sensing behavior of hierarchical tri-phase carbon nanotube systems across a wide temperature range (from -170°C (-274°F) to 90°C (194°F)). The study has been published in the Carbon journal.

phys-org.title: Early career funding improves scientific influence and citations for women
phys-org.description: Early-career funding has a bigger impact on women than men when it comes to their careers in science, according to a new study from City St George's, University of London. While the study found that successful applicants in both groups secure more future research funding than unsuccessful applicants, it also found that successful female applicants receive more citations and are cited more often in their field than female applicants who did not receive funding.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s Rightward Turn
proj-syn.description: There is a growing tension in Colombia between the popular demand for a strong welfare state and a political system that cannot deliver on that promise unless it breaks free from malign influences. Since the incoming administration is aligned with many of those interests, Colombians will continue to be disappointed.

proj-syn.title: A Cold War Adventure in Portugal
proj-syn.description: Just 52 years after escaping military dictatorship, Portugal is an EU and eurozone member and the world’s seventh-safest country. While Donald Trump's systematic destruction of the rules-based global order will not reverse this progress, nor will it do any good for Portugal, the US, or anyone else.

proj-syn.title: Social-Media Age Bans Won’t Make Children Safer—But This Will
proj-syn.description: As the European Union considers how to protect and empower young people in a digital world, it must resist the urge only to enact a ban on social media for young people. A more effective strategy would force tech companies to remove addictive features by holding them to product-liability standards—as with most other industries.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Sit Atop the Next World Order?
proj-syn.description: American hegemony has given way to a global order based on rivalry and competition among several major powers, where there is no longer a fixed, codified set of rules. Instead, there is only economic, technological, and military power—the likes of which China is amassing faster than many observers realize.

proj-syn.title: AI Will Supercharge Surveillance Capitalism
proj-syn.description: For too long, governments have stood by and allowed the creation of business models built on the commercial exploitation of users' personal data and that reward social and psychological manipulation. With the AI industry poised to replicate this model, policymakers must intervene before it is too late.

proj-syn.title: An Alternative History for America at 250
proj-syn.description: Commemorating the 250th anniversary of the United States requires an honest appraisal of not only its founding principles but also its racist and imperialist legacy. A clear-eyed assessment shows why many people in the Global South remain cynical about the country’s ability to live up to its ideals.

proj-syn.title: A Turning Point for African Industrialization
proj-syn.description: Building on the success of his mega-refinery in Lagos, Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote is in talks to construct a second one in collaboration with several East African countries. African leaders should learn from Dangote’s strategy of adding value to the continent’s natural resources and fostering cross-border cooperation.

proj-syn.title: Subsidies Do Not Explain China’s Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: Like every major economy, China uses industrial policy, and its subsidies have mattered. But subsidies are no longer the most convincing explanation for Chinese firms’ emergence as global leaders in industries that used to be the exclusive domain of advanced economies.

proj-syn.title: Putin Likes His Worst Option in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: Faced with a quagmire in eastern Ukraine and escalating Ukrainian attacks within Russia, Vladimir Putin must either seek a ceasefire or pursue some form of escalation. With all signs pointing to him embracing the latter alternative, the situation could worsen dramatically for everyone, but especially for him.

proj-syn.title: The Subversion of the International Criminal Court
proj-syn.description: Already under US sanctions for his role in securing an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court is now at risk of being removed altogether. If member states do not stand up for judicial independence now, they may never get another chance.

proj-syn.title: What Inequality Does to Electoral Democracy
proj-syn.description: Like many advanced democracies, France has long cycled between periods in which its politics were divided along traditional left-right redistributionist lines, and those in which culture war issues took center stage. If there is any lesson to be drawn from this history, it is that the cycle may be about to repeat.

proj-syn.title: Where Will Global Financial Fragmentation Lead?
proj-syn.description: Debates about geopolitical fragmentation always revive the late economist Robert Mundell’s dream of a single world money. But participants should be mindful of the euro’s real-world experience over the past quarter-century.

proj-syn.title: Development Economics for an Age of Upheaval
proj-syn.description: The framework that has long guided development economics no longer reflects how modern economies actually create value. As the boundaries that once separated sectors become blurred, prosperity increasingly depends on how economies build the ecosystems that sustain technological progress and nurture new productive capacity.

proj-syn.title: The Death of the Degree
proj-syn.description: AI is often portrayed as a threat to higher education, with some administrators and professors focused on rooting out its use. But this approach fails to recognize that, in an AI-transformed world, the new dividing lines are technical capabilities and institutional pipelines that can quickly transform research into products.

proj-syn.title: Hungary’s Real Economic Test
proj-syn.description: Entering the euro with favorable market sentiment, but without an economy that can function well within a monetary union, would not serve Hungary’s long-term interests. It would be a formula for more broken promises—precisely the trend that the new government was elected to end.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Exposes the Global Economy’s Fault Lines
proj-syn.description: Buoyed by AI stocks, global financial markets have largely shrugged off the war with Iran. Yet the conflict’s long-term economic costs are only beginning to emerge, as depleted strategic oil reserves, damaged refining capacity, and rising fuel and fertilizer costs increasingly weigh on lower-income economies.

proj-syn.title: Governments Should Govern AI, Not Own It
proj-syn.description: AI systems are now powerful enough to threaten critical infrastructure, financial systems, and national security. Rather than becoming shareholders in AI companies, as US President Donald Trump has proposed, governments should invest in the independent institutions needed to hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: The Tragedy of “Westalgia”
proj-syn.description: Some European leaders seem to think that abasing themselves for Donald Trump's pleasure is necessary to save NATO and keep the Western alliance alive. But by so desperately clinging to the good old days of the transatlantic relationship, Europe’s leaders are risking more than just their dignity.
